reason: The sole cited evidence (E1) only mentions that 'anti-oxidation coatings are still required' for Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys, which is a general suggestion, not specific prior evidence. It provides no data on alumina-forming coatings, their application to HfNbTaTiZr, their effectiveness as an oxygen barrier, or their impact on mechanical properties. Thus, none of the key premises are supported by the cited passage.
premises: A thin alumina-forming coating can be applied to cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will form a continuous, adherent, thermally stable Al2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
The Al2O3 scale will greatly retard oxygen diffusion into the substrate.
Limiting oxidation will preserve the bulk microstructure responsible for mechanical performance.
The coating will not compromise room-temperature ductility or high-temperature yield strength.
